findings.description: `_existing` turns `'\''` back into `'` using a double-quoted pattern substitution whose replacement is the literal `\'`. Bash 4.3+ strips the backslash from that replacement, so the decode works there. Bash 4.2 and older do not (bash's own compat42 notes say so), and that includes macOS's `/bin/bash` 3.2. The template supports macOS (`open_url` falls back to `open`), and `#!/usr/bin/env bash` picks up 3.2 when Homebrew bash isn't installed. On that bash, a value containing `'` that `write_env` saved comes back as `\'`. It is shown as the "[Enter keeps current]" default, and pressing Enter makes `write_env` re-encode and save the corrupted value. Each re-run adds another backslash.
findings.body:
**On bash ≤ 4.2 (macOS `/bin/bash`), `_existing` decodes `'` wrongly, so each re-run corrupts the stored value**

`write_env` stores `'` as `'\''`, and `_existing` turns it back with `"${value//"$sq"/\'}"`. In a double-quoted expansion, bash 4.3+ removes the backslash from the replacement `\'`. Bash ≤ 4.2 keeps it. Bash's COMPAT notes for `compat42` say: *"the replacement string in double-quoted pattern substitution does not undergo quote removal"*.

macOS still ships bash 3.2 as `/bin/bash`, and the template targets macOS (`open_url` falls back to `open`). Nothing else in the template needs bash 4, so it runs there and hits this:

1. `write_env K "it's"` stores `K='it'\''s'`.
2. `_existing` returns `it\'s`.
3. The prompt offers it as `[Enter keeps current]`. Pressing Enter saves `'it\'\''s'`.
4. Every later run adds another backslash.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/c67c0af401a9b0583c61f94ca647e3cd2764600e/.claude/skills/wizard/template.sh#L96-L98

Taking the replacement from a variable makes it decode the same way on every bash version. Text that comes out of an expansion never goes through quote removal. `$q` has no `&`, so bash 5.2's `patsub_replacement` leaves it alone too. `write_env` already uses `$sq` the same way on the encode side.

This file is taken whole from upstream, so the fix may belong upstream too.
findings.suggestion:
local line value sq="'\\''" q="'"; line=$(grep -E "^${1}=" "$ENV_FILE" | tail -n1) || return 1
  value="${line#*=}"
  if [[ "$value" == \'*\' ]]; then value="${value:1:${#value}-2}"; value="${value//"$sq"/$q}"

findings.description: `write_env` used to `mv` a 0600 `mktemp` file over `.env`, so any write left `.env` at 0600. It now writes through `cat` and keeps the existing mode. A `.env` copied from `.env.example` under umask 022 stays world-readable (0644) after secrets are written to it. Adding `chmod go-rwx "$ENV_FILE"` after the `cat` keeps the symlink write-through and tightens the mode.

If `cat "$tmp" > "$ENV_FILE"` fails (for example, the user made `.env` read-only, which the old `mv` tolerated), `set -e` aborts before `rm -f "$tmp"`. That leaves a 0600 copy of the whole `.env`, new secret included, in `$TMPDIR`. A `trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' RETURN` in `write_env` would clean it up.

`write_env` now writes `KEY='value'` and escapes `'` as `'\''`. Only a shell understands that escape: node `dotenv` and `python-dotenv` read `KEY='it'\''s'` as `it` plus trailing junk. The old unquoted form passed such values through intact. Quoting still fixes values with spaces or `#`, so this only bites apostrophe values read by a non-shell `.env` reader.

With no tracker, the skill points at tickets in `docs/plans/<feature-slug>/issues/` and tells it to pass subagents context pointers to them. `docs/plans/` is local-only (`scripts/pre-commit` refuses to commit it), so the files exist only in the main checkout, not on the integration branch the per-ticket worktrees branch from. A relative pointer handed to an implementer won't resolve. One clause saying no-tracker pointers use absolute paths into the main checkout would fix it.

Step 2 says the transcript directory is the project path "with `/` replaced by `-`". Claude Code actually replaces every non-alphanumeric character with `-`. In this repo's required `.worktrees/<name>` checkouts the real directory is `...--worktrees-<name>`, so following the rule literally gives a path that doesn't exist (`...-.worktrees-<name>`).

process_issues.description: review-context was not spawned. The diff touches no CI, HTTP, docker or settings surfaces, only skill prose, one shell template, READMEs and the social-preview asset. Instance scaling was also held at one per area even though the PR has 16 files across 3 top-level areas: the only executable logic is a single file (`wizard/template.sh`, about 65 changed lines), so splitting it across instances would have overlapped.

The review-validator reported that `git diff <merge_base>..HEAD` asked for approval and could not run, so it fell back to `gh pr diff`. It also could not run bash 3.2 or 4.2, so the bash-version finding rests on the documented COMPAT behaviour rather than an executed test (confidence medium).
